sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A debrief of Neo4j's Relate, and how it compares with our graphs as JSON in encrypted, versioned vaults.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: What Relate is; well made for its shape; where it does not fit; our graphs; each wins; together in LETS.

sections.label: What Relate is
sections.line: Embedded Rust graph database: openCypher, vectors, full-text, MCP, agent CLI, WASM, seven languages.

sections.label: Where it fits, in its own words
sections.line: One app, one machine, in memory, one writer; no TLS, one shared credential, no roles.

sections.label: How we keep graphs
sections.line: Graphs as JSON files in sgit vaults: encrypted, one GET per file, versioned, many writers, nothing running.

sections.label: Side by side
sections.line: Relate wins at traversals, Cypher, transactions and agent ergonomics; we win at encryption, history, writers, size.

sections.label: Better together
sections.line: Relate is the right shape for the Transform step of Load, Extract, Transform, Save.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not benchmarked; our numbers from sgit.ai; different work; the combination is a proposal.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Neo4j's press release, relatedb.ai docs, sgit.ai's performance page and earlier articles.
